answer: One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism in an agent economy is a stake-weighted attestation bridge that forces attackers to mirror real economic cost. By requiring agents to lock tokens proportional to their claimed influence, a sudden gale of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive; each duplicate must burn or lock value that cannot be cheaply recycled, so the attacker pays real capital rather than just spinning up free accounts. Peers then verify the stake proof before counting votes, making mass identity farming uneconomic.
